sources.title: Bioretention Design Handbook: Designing Holistic Bioretention for Performance and Longevity
sources.locator: Ch. 4 §4.1, pp. 4-2–4-3; Ch. 6 §§6.3–6.6; Ch. 7 §7.3; Ch. 13; Ch. 14 §14.2. Critic browser rendering also inspected the opening scope, drainage-area delineation/grade, inlet, and leaf-screen/pretreatment passages.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official EPA NEPIS text, reviewed its scope and relevant chapter passages, and searched within the text for drainage-area delineation, undersized inlets, historical inlet changes, and leaf pretreatment. No design calculation or field work was performed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The handbook says site conditions and local requirements govern design selection. Capture and runoff volumes depend on delineated drainage area, flow direction/grade and inlet configuration. It describes alternatives and historical examples, not universal fixes; pretreatment has maintenance implications.
sources.applicability_and_limits: Supports the draft's records-first inquiry and conditional alternatives. It does not supply the hypothetical site's drainage boundary, elevations, inlet condition, or an applicable construction dimension.
sources.issue_fix_regression_release_history: Static 2023 edition. The accessed handbook describes site-specific inlet problems and changes; no later revision or errata was established in this review.

sources.title: Operation and maintenance of bioretention and other stormwater infiltration practices
sources.publisher: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, Minnesota Stormwater Manual
sources.released_version_or_commit: Living manual page; no current page revision/date was visible in the reviewed rendering.
sources.locator: Post-construction maintenance table and troubleshooting table, especially mulch note and rows for standing water, blocked flow path, and inlet scour; rendered around lines 178–212.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official MPCA page and reviewed the rendered tables and mulch note. No site inspection or maintenance was performed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The maintenance table places a 48-hour post-rain check in a semiannual after-first-year schedule and says deep sumps may retain water. The troubleshooting table describes standing water over 48 hours as a symptom with possible sediment/pretreatment causes, and leaves/debris as possible blockage; mulch can clog inlets, outlets, or bypass pipes. These are contextual possibilities and recommendations, not a universal site criterion.
sources.applicability_and_limits: Supports logging debris, mulch, sediment, maintenance, and ponding while preserving uncertainty. Minnesota guidance does not establish this site's local criterion or diagnose the hypothetical garden.
sources.issue_fix_regression_release_history: No dated page revision or issue/fix history was visible in the live rendering.

sources.title: Overview for bioretention
sources.publisher: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, Minnesota Stormwater Manual
sources.released_version_or_commit: Living manual page; no page revision or commit was displayed.
sources.locator: Water quantity treatment / high-flow bypass section, rendered lines 106–116.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official MPCA page and searched/reviewed the offline and maximum-ponding-depth passages. No design calculation was performed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The page describes high-flow bypass when a cell fills to maximum ponding depth; it prefers offline designs where feasible to reduce internal erosion, and recommends short high-flow paths and energy dissipation where relevant. Actual layout remains site-dependent.
sources.applicability_and_limits: Supports keeping intended bypass, overflow, and downstream route distinct. It does not show whether bypass at this site is intended or excessive.
sources.issue_fix_regression_release_history: The live page links a June 2022 PDF snapshot; no current live-page revision was shown.

sources.title: Alleviating compaction from construction activities
sources.publisher: Minnesota Pollution Control Agency, Minnesota Stormwater Manual
sources.released_version_or_commit: Living manual page; no current revision identifier was visible in the reviewed rendering.
sources.locator: Causes/effects and determining extent of compaction, rendered lines 103–132; method-effectiveness and applicability, lines 222–265.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official MPCA page and read the cause/effect, observation/measurement, and restoration-limit passages. No compaction measurement or infiltration test was performed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The page identifies equipment, stockpiling and traffic as causes and wet/clay soils as more susceptible. Ponding is one possible observation, not proof; field measurements have method limits. It says restoration must be tailored and does not recommend a prescriptive specification.
sources.applicability_and_limits: Makes delivery-related compaction a plausible inquiry only. No site condition or soil property is established by this general guidance.
sources.issue_fix_regression_release_history: The page references a changing research base and reports variation in remediation evidence; no live-page revision history was visible.

sources.title: Evaluating Green Infrastructure Stormwater Capture Performance under Extreme Precipitation
sources.publisher: Journal of Extreme Events; author record hosted by Drexel University; World Scientific Publishing
sources.released_version_or_commit: Journal of Extreme Events, volume 3 issue 2, article 1650006, June 2016.
sources.locator: Article abstract, especially study conditions and findings, rendered lines 22–29; bibliographic details lines 5–13 and 55–63.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the university-hosted peer-reviewed article record and read its abstract and publication metadata. The full article was not reviewed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The abstract describes one Queens facility with sandy native soil and low 3.8:1 loading ratio; its inlet bypass often limited capture despite high infiltration. Duration, precipitation total, and peak-hour intensity were associated with capture at that site. Maintenance frequency was described as anecdotal and for future investigation.
sources.applicability_and_limits: Supports distinguishing capture from infiltration and recording storm covariates. Its geometry, soil, capture percentages, and causal relationships are not predictive for this hypothetical site.
sources.issue_fix_regression_release_history: Static 2016 journal article record; no correction history was identified in the accessed record.

sources.locator: Official publication record/abstract. Detailed report section “Performance on an Event Basis” was not independently read in this critic review.
sources.observed_operation: Queried the official USGS Publications Warehouse and reviewed the returned report metadata and abstract. A direct browser open of the record/PDF returned an internal error, so no detailed report text or event table is claimed as independently checked.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: The official record describes two monitored Omaha gardens; volume reduction varied by event size at one garden, and no overflow was recorded at the other. These are results from the measured sites, not general design thresholds.
sources.applicability_and_limits: Supports an example of event-dependent behavior only. The critic did not independently verify the draft's specific similar-depth/different-duration event examples; the report's numeric results do not transfer to this unmeasured case.
sources.issue_fix_regression_release_history: Static numbered-series USGS report issued in 2016; no later correction/version history was identified in the reviewed publication record.
